decisions.summary: a builder is any agent whose agent_type names no .claude/agents file - every defined agent exempt, where the spec exempts a defined REVIEW agent
decisions.why: The spec's own exclusion, made mechanical. As the plan states (R3, not in the bundle), the rule caught every builder that passed the cap in the window. It would only reach too little if some defined agent that is not a reviewer were dispatched with a task's brief. If such an agent exists in .claude/agents, it must be capped too.

decisions.summary: a general-purpose agent dispatched with no task is capped too
decisions.why: It narrows nothing. The test is structural, so a builder cannot escape the cap through how its brief is worded, which is the real-enforcement reading. As the plan states, every general-purpose dispatch is a brief.

decisions.summary: context_cap_hooks refuses a builder's every call past CONTEXT_CAP_TOKENS (GUESS 300k) but the handoff Write; CONTEXT_OK or a recorded make context-ok permit escapes
decisions.why: FR-006 and FR-012. The knob is the spec's GUESS. The handoff Write is tested through the whole guard chain.

decisions.summary: SendMessage to a builder past the cap refused
decisions.why: FR-006 as written.

decisions.summary: SendMessage to a builder whose task has landed: the task is taken ONLY from the meta description's T<n>
decisions.why: FR-006 says a SendMessage resuming a builder whose task has landed is refused. D8 itself says a builder with an unnamed brief exists and must not slip through. Yet D10 finds the task only from a T<n> in the description, so for that builder the landed-task refusal never fires, and its resume leaves no record. Working out the task is not impossible: D2 already has a fallback chain (the task the agent's lines carry, else the clone's task-starts entry at its dispatch). Fix: D10 uses D2's chain, and a builder with any landing of its task after its dispatch is refused, with a red case for a builder whose description names no T<n>.

decisions.summary: every session's and agent's make static runs count toward the task, the main session's too
decisions.why: FR-007 counts runs in one task and names no agent.

decisions.summary: the count window starts at the later of the task's last task-starts entry and its last landing
decisions.why: FR-007 has one reset: 'since its last landing'. Lines are already filtered by task, so a start bound adds nothing except a second reset, and the plan gives no reason for it. Whether an open task can gain a second task-starts entry is unmeasured. If it can, running task-start again zeroes the count with no recorded escape, which turns the refusal into an instruction. Fix: count the task's static lines since its last landing only (or since its FIRST start where it has never landed), with a red case where a second task-start does not reset the count.

decisions.summary: a make or cargo run backgrounded with & and then waited on in the same call passes
decisions.why: The approved fix targets a run whose end no notice reports ('no completion notice came, and it sat idle'). A call that waits on its job does not return before the run ends, so the harness tracks it. Refusing it would refuse a tracked run and serve none of the rule's purpose.

decisions.summary: the pass test is 'no wait later in the command': no command position for wait, and nothing ties the wait to the make job
decisions.why: D12a's reason holds only for a wait that covers the make job, but the plan's test is any later 'wait'. Under it, `make static & echo wait` and `make static & sleep 5 & wait $!` (which waits only for the sleep) both pass, return with the run detached, and leave no record: exactly T225's untracked run. The plan already asks command position for nohup, setsid and disown, and asks none for wait. Fix: pass only a wait at a command position that covers the make or cargo job (a bare wait, or wait $!/%N naming that job with no & between), with red cases for the two forms above.

decisions.summary: main session only (no agent_id), on both permitted no-poll paths including the POLL_OK-escaped loop, longest sleep over POLL_CHECK_S (GUESS 60 s) refused; SLOW_POLL_OK escapes
decisions.why: FR-008 as written. POLL_OK does not bypass it.

decisions.summary: knobs recorded as GUESS constants and a docs/guards.md knob table; make tunables not extended to the tooling crates
decisions.why: The GM's request names no knob register and no make tunables, and no cited FR does either, so leaving tunables as it is narrows nothing asked. The spec's Assumptions text was not in the bundle, so this rests on the plan's statement that the spec names tunables only as where retuning happens.

decisions.summary: a deferral must carry a reason, 'a task id T<n>' and 'lands before T<n>' - checked as a form, not as a FILED task
decisions.why: FR-009 asks for 'its filed task id'. The plan checks for a string T<n>, so a made-up id that is in no tasks.md passes make decide with no record: a form check where the request asked for real enforcement. Checking it is cheap (the feature's tasks.md and tasks-done.md). Fix: the deferral's T<n>, and its lands-before T<n>, must name tasks filed in the feature, with a red case for an unfiled id.

decisions.summary: a class-of-defect fix must carry an observed-date-and-method line
decisions.why: FR-009's second clause as written.

decisions.summary: make land splits T= on commas and whitespace
decisions.why: FR-011, the approved 'Accept commas in T='.

decisions.summary: task-add: if quick is still red after withdrawing the line, the line is restored and the run only reports - no comparison of failures
decisions.why: FR-011 refuses 'on any failure the new line introduces'. When make quick is already red for another reason, a line that adds a failure of its own is restored and passes with no record (T19's third case pins this). It is not impossible to catch: compare the failures with the line to those without it. Fix: refuse and withdraw whenever the with-line run has a failure the without-line run lacks, and keep the line only when the failures are the same; add a red case with a pre-existing failure plus the line's own.

decisions.summary: suites split into numbered shards, the runner stamps the suite when every shard is green, SHARD_BAR_S GUESS about 20 s measured, never a gate
decisions.why: FR-010 and SC-004.

decisions.summary: Resume refused for a builder past the cap or whose task SUCCESSFULLY landed (end code 0 naming it, or ticked or archived) after dispatch. The task is found by meta T<n>, else its FIRST line's task, else the task-starts entry in force at dispatch.
decisions.why: FR-006 as written. The revision closes what the last round raised: no description-only lookup, the first line rather than the latest, the entry in force at dispatch, a background landing found through its end line's tasks, a refused landing not counted. T13 carries a red case for each of these.

decisions.summary: When no task can be found anywhere (no T<n>, no line carrying one, no task-starts entry before dispatch), the resume passes and 'context-cap: resume, no task' is written to the guard log.
decisions.why: Physically impossible: with no task there is nothing to test for having landed. It is only reachable when the feature had no task-start before the dispatch, because D2 stamps every later line with the active task. The pass leaves a record. LEGITIMATE only for the landed half. A builder past the cap with no task is still refused, because the bullet does not reach the cap. The plan should say so, and T13 should carry a case for it (see the D15 entry's list).

decisions.summary: static_runs_hooks counts a task's make static PreToolUse lines (every session and agent) since its last SUCCESSFUL landing, else since its FIRST task-start; a later task-start resets nothing; the third is refused naming the delta's crate-scoped checks; STATIC_OK escapes; knob GUESS 2.
decisions.why: FR-007 literally: 'a third make static in one task since its last landing'. It counts by task, so the main session's runs count too. The revision removes the last round's unrecorded resets (a second task-start, a refused landing), and T14 carries a red case for each.

decisions.summary: A make or cargo job followed by & is refused unless a wait that COVERS it follows: at a command position, in the same list and shell, unconditional, not backgrounded, and bare, wait $! with no & between, or wait %N. nohup/setsid/disown at a command position are refused. A saved-pid wait is refused. DETACH_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-008 lists & with no exception. But the approved fix was 'a guard refusing that pattern', meaning T225's detached run whose end the session never learned of. A covering wait keeps the Bash call open until the run ends, so the harness tracks it. The exception is implied by the request's own words, and refusing it would serve no part of the request's purpose. The revision makes 'covers' real: words, other shells, conditional waits, a backgrounded wait and a stale $! are all refused, each with a T15 red case. Refusing the saved-pid form is stricter than FR-008 and is within it. Notes, not blocking: wait %N has no case either way in T15; setsid and disown have no firing case (only nohup does); and whether D1 sees '{ ...; } &', 'VAR=x make ... &' or 'env ... make &' cannot be judged from this bundle, so T02 or T15 should pin those forms.

decisions.summary: On both permitted no-poll paths, a main-session (no agent_id) loop whose longest sleep exceeds POLL_CHECK_S (GUESS 60 s) is refused naming the 60 s form; SLOW_POLL_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-008's second clause. It turns the approved 'shorter poll loop on my side' into a refusal, as 'real enforcement' asks. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Knobs carry GUESS at their point of change and a knob table in docs/guards.md; make tunables is not extended to the tooling crates.
decisions.why: The GM's request never mentions make tunables. Its mention is a spec Assumption about where retuning happens, and the knob table (knob, value, label, the data that retunes it) serves the same purpose. Unchanged since the last reading, so the ruling stands.

decisions.summary: deferral_unformed: a non-none Found-and-left item must carry a reason, a task id and 'lands before T<n>', both ids FILED in the feature (a box of tasks.md OR an entry of tasks-done.md); a class fix needs an 'observed <date>, method:' line; DEFER_FORM_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-009 asks for 'its filed task id and its order ("lands before ...")', so that a deferred defect actually gets fixed, and in a known order (the approved 'briefs that default to fixing in the task'). Accepting an entry of tasks-done.md, which T17's second variant passes on purpose, guts both. (a) An order 'lands before T124' where T124 has already landed cannot be kept, so it orders nothing. (b) A deferral to a task that is already done will never be fixed by that task. Any feature has dozens of done ids, so a done id passes the check as easily as the made-up id the last round flagged: the hole has moved, not closed. That is a word-level reading of 'filed' that is fatal to the rule's purpose. Required, all in one revision: (1) at make decide, when the item is judged, both ids must name an OPEN task (an unticked box in the feature's tasks.md), and a section already decided is not refused later because an id it named has since landed; (2) the order's id differs from the deferral's own task id ('T123 lands before T123' is refused); (3) T17 drops the passing tasks-done variant and adds refused cases for a done deferral id, a done order id and a self-order, plus the case T17's own heading names and its list lacks: a reason and a filed task id with no 'lands before' at all, refused. Also, from D10-no-task: say that a builder past the cap with no task is still refused, and add that case to T13.

decisions.summary: land splits T= on commas and whitespace. task-add runs quick's check lines (from make -n quick) each to its own end, with and without the line, compares the findings as a multiset with line and column numbers masked, refuses and withdraws on any new finding, and restores the line only when the findings are identical; QUICK_OK escapes.
decisions.why: FR-011 as written. 'On any failure the new line introduces, withdraws the line and refuses' now holds even when an earlier check is already red or a finding in the same file is shifted, and T19 carries a red case for each. Restoring the line when the findings are the same is FR-011's own boundary (the line introduced no failure), not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Hook suites may be sharded as test-<name>.<k>.sh, stamped green when every shard is; entry-gate split by its two cases, the other two by case groups to about 20 s or less (SHARD_BAR_S GUESS, measured, never a gate).
